ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PAKPAK BHARAT REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Pakpak Bharat Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pakpak Bharat.
4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Social Service is the Social Service of Pakpak Bharat Regency. 6. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnicity, group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief resulting in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including those in the womb.
9. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act that results in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and demeans the dignity of the child carried out by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, for example parents, close family, teachers and companions.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims covering physical, psychological, and sexual health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social function naturally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin.
16. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively covering information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
21. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
22. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children and mother and her children.
24. Household is family members and relatives such as grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, husband, wife, cousins and so on and non-relatives such as domestic workers, drivers and so on who live and reside in one house.
25. Local wisdom is truth that has become traditional or established in a region, local wisdom is a combination of sacred religious values and various existing values. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id

Article 14

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of regional apparatus units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

Article 8

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 7

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 5 letter b, are carried out in the form of community participation. (2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing acts of violence against women and children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties;
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence; d. providing protection to victims; and
e. providing emergency assistance. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id

Article 18

(1) The Regent shall provide guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM in the Field of Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence in the Region.

(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include the provision of implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of services for women and children victims of violence.

Article 17

Funding for the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence shall be sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 2

Letter a

The principle of humanity serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity and worth of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (second principle of Pancasila)

Letter b

The principle of gender equality and justice, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, and governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter c

The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Letter d

The principle of protection of victims' rights, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, the community and the Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as stipulated in laws and regulations.

Letter e

The principle of legal certainty is the best interest of women and children, constitutes a principle specific to women and children themselves such as for example, how the interests of child victims of violence to undergo sanctions imposed jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id on them, or how children will face perpetrators in court proceedings, must be stated in accordance with the interests of child victims of violence.

Likewise for women victims of violence who wish to be given freedom in accordance with their interests, women who wish to forget the perpetrator who is nota bene a person they once loved, and so on. Thus we as a community or as law enforcement officers need to provide opportunities for children and women to express their interests regarding everything related to the perpetrator as well as how to overcome the impact of violence that befalls them.

Article 6

Regional Action Plan is the program and activity stages of the implementation of protection of women and children victims of acts of violence including the worst forms of work for children that must be carried out by Regional Work Units in accordance with their duties and functions, prepared based on achievement targets within a period of 5 (five) years.

CHAPTER V

PREVENTION OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 19

In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the community may:

a. form family partners at the village level by the community; b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims;
d. participate with the authorized agencies when violence against victims occurs in their environment.
e. community participation shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id

Article 16

(1) The Regent shall be responsible for making a report on the implementation of SPM in the field of integrated services for women and children victims of violence to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.

(2) The reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of regional apparatus units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

Letter b

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse, hurtful comments that even demean self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening/intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

What is meant by "sexual violence" is violence against sexuality which includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or disregarding the satisfaction of the wife.

Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against persons residing within the household sphere, forced sexual intercourse of someone within their household sphere with other persons for commercial purposes and or specific purposes.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

Letter a

The principle of humanity serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity and worth of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (second principle of Pancasila)

Letter b

The principle of gender equality and justice, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, and governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter c

The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Letter d

The principle of protection of victims' rights, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, the community and the Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as stipulated in laws and regulations.

Letter e

The principle of legal certainty is the best interest of women and children, constitutes a principle specific to women and children themselves such as for example, how the interests of child victims of violence to undergo sanctions imposed jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id on them, or how children will face perpetrators in court proceedings, must be stated in accordance with the interests of child victims of violence.

Likewise for women victims of violence who wish to be given freedom in accordance with their interests, women who wish to forget the perpetrator who is nota bene a person they once loved, and so on. Thus we as a community or as law enforcement officers need to provide opportunities for children and women to express their interests regarding everything related to the perpetrator as well as how to overcome the impact of violence that befalls them.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 8

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 7

(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 5 letter b, are carried out in the form of community participation. (2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:

a. preventing acts of violence against women and children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties;
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence; d. providing protection to victims; and
e. providing emergency assistance. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id

Article 2

Letter a

The principle of humanity serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity and worth of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (second principle of Pancasila)

Letter b

The principle of gender equality and justice, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, and governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter c

The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Letter d

The principle of protection of victims' rights, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, the community and the Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as stipulated in laws and regulations.

Letter e

The principle of legal certainty is the best interest of women and children, constitutes a principle specific to women and children themselves such as for example, how the interests of child victims of violence to undergo sanctions imposed jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id on them, or how children will face perpetrators in court proceedings, must be stated in accordance with the interests of child victims of violence.

Likewise for women victims of violence who wish to be given freedom in accordance with their interests, women who wish to forget the perpetrator who is nota bene a person they once loved, and so on. Thus we as a community or as law enforcement officers need to provide opportunities for children and women to express their interests regarding everything related to the perpetrator as well as how to overcome the impact of violence that befalls them.

Article 18

(1) The Regent shall provide guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM in the Field of Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence in the Region.

(2) The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include the provision of implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of services for women and children victims of violence.

Article 17

Funding for the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence shall be sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER III

VICTIMS' RIGHTS

Article 15

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children shall be conducted every evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary as needed.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 6

Regional Action Plan is the program and activity stages of the implementation of protection of women and children victims of acts of violence including the worst forms of work for children that must be carried out by Regional Work Units in accordance with their duties and functions, prepared based on achievement targets within a period of 5 (five) years.

Article 19

In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the community may:

a. form family partners at the village level by the community; b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims;
d. participate with the authorized agencies when violence against victims occurs in their environment.
e. community participation shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id

7. 11. 22. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 3

Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/tugging hair, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons and or resulting in bodily disability of a person, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.

Letter b

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse, hurtful comments that even demean self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening/intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is violence against sexuality which includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or disregarding the satisfaction of the wife.

Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against persons residing within the household sphere, forced sexual intercourse of someone within their household sphere with other persons for commercial purposes and or specific purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "Economic Neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife and children or family or relatives such as not providing maintenance to the wife or spending the wife's money, not providing or withholding wages of domestic workers and drivers including acts of limiting or prohibiting family members from engaging in decent work.

Letter e

What is meant by "Restriction of movement" is restricting the freedom of movement of the wife or children to develop their potential both for economic jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id and social purposes such as prohibiting gathering or socializing with the community as well as restricting the space of relatives such as preventing domestic workers and drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Pakpak Bharat Regency.

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

CHAPTER III

VICTIMS' RIGHTS

1.10.text:
Article 3

Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/tugging hair, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons and or resulting in bodily disability of a person, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.

Letter b

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse, hurtful comments that even demean self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening/intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is violence against sexuality which includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or disregarding the satisfaction of the wife.

Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against persons residing within the household sphere, forced sexual intercourse of someone within their household sphere with other persons for commercial purposes and or specific purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "Economic Neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife and children or family or relatives such as not providing maintenance to the wife or spending the wife's money, not providing or withholding wages of domestic workers and drivers including acts of limiting or prohibiting family members from engaging in decent work.

Letter e

What is meant by "Restriction of movement" is restricting the freedom of movement of the wife or children to develop their potential both for economic jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id and social purposes such as prohibiting gathering or socializing with the community as well as restricting the space of relatives such as preventing domestic workers and drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

Article 8

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Pakpak Bharat Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pakpak Bharat.
4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Social Service is the Social Service of Pakpak Bharat Regency. 6. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnicity, group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief resulting in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including those in the womb.
9. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act that results in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and demeans the dignity of the child carried out by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, for example parents, close family, teachers and companions.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims covering physical, psychological, and sexual health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social function naturally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin.
16. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively covering information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
21. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
22. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children and mother and her children.
24. Household is family members and relatives such as grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, husband, wife, cousins and so on and non-relatives such as domestic workers, drivers and so on who live and reside in one house.
25. Local wisdom is truth that has become traditional or established in a region, local wisdom is a combination of sacred religious values and various existing values. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id

Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Pakpak Bharat Regency.

CHAPTER V

PREVENTION OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

Article 19

In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the community may:

a. form family partners at the village level by the community; b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims;

CONCERNING

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Pakpak Bharat Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the regional government administration that leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pakpak Bharat.
4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Social Service is the Social Service of Pakpak Bharat Regency. 6. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnicity, group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political belief resulting in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including those in the womb.
9. Violence is any unlawful act with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any act that results in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and demeans the dignity of the child carried out by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, for example parents, close family, teachers and companions.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims covering physical, psychological, and sexual health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social function naturally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin.
16. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that provides integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively covering information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
21. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
22. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children and mother and her children.
24. Household is family members and relatives such as grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfather, grandmother, husband, wife, cousins and so on and non-relatives such as domestic workers, drivers and so on who live and reside in one house.
25. Local wisdom is truth that has become traditional or established in a region, local wisdom is a combination of sacred religious values and various existing values. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id

Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF PAKPAK BHARAT REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

Letter a

The principle of humanity serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity and worth of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (second principle of Pancasila)

The principle of gender equality and justice, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, and governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter c

The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Letter d

The principle of protection of victims' rights, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, the community and the Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as stipulated in laws and regulations.

Likewise for women victims of violence who wish to be given freedom in accordance with their interests, women who wish to forget the perpetrator who is nota bene a person they once loved, and so on. Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/tugging hair, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons and or resulting in bodily disability of a person, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.

Letter b

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse, hurtful comments that even demean self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening/intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is violence against sexuality which includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or disregarding the satisfaction of the wife.

Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against persons residing within the household sphere, forced sexual intercourse of someone within their household sphere with other persons for commercial purposes and or specific purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "Economic Neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife and children or family or relatives such as not providing maintenance to the wife or spending the wife's money, not providing or withholding wages of domestic workers and drivers including acts of limiting or prohibiting family members from engaging in decent work.

Letter e

What is meant by "Restriction of movement" is restricting the freedom of movement of the wife or children to develop their potential both for economic jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id and social purposes such as prohibiting gathering or socializing with the community as well as restricting the space of relatives such as preventing domestic workers and drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

NUMBER 2 OF 2017

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble to the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph, include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all of Indonesia's territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) educating the life of the nation and (4) participating in implementing world order based on

(a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice. The State of the Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, but in reality there are still many women and children who are victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation under it.

Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, communities, the nation and the state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Human Trafficking. Protection for women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of the Regional Government as stipulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy, regions have the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, national unity and harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

On that basis, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially for women and children jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation on the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of the Regional Regulation on the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, the handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of preventing and handling violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in preventing violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

Letter b

The principle of gender equality and justice, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, and governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter c

The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

Letter d

The principle of protection of victims' rights, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, the community and the Regional Government to fulfill the rights of women and children who are victims of acts of violence as stipulated in laws and regulations.

Letter e

The principle of legal certainty is the best interest of women and children, constitutes a principle specific to women and children themselves such as for example, how the interests of child victims of violence to undergo sanctions imposed jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id on them, or how children will face perpetrators in court proceedings, must be stated in accordance with the interests of child victims of violence.

Likewise for women victims of violence who wish to be given freedom in accordance with their interests, women who wish to forget the perpetrator who is nota bene a person they once loved, and so on. Thus we as a community or as law enforcement officers need to provide opportunities for children and women to express their interests regarding everything related to the perpetrator as well as how to overcome the impact of violence that befalls them.

Article 3

Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting, pulling hair/tugging hair, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons and or resulting in bodily disability of a person, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.

Letter b

What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse, hurtful comments that even demean self-esteem, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening/intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.

Letter c

What is meant by "sexual violence" is violence against sexuality which includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her spiritual needs, forcing sexual intercourse, forcing one's own sexual preferences or disregarding the satisfaction of the wife.

Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual intercourse committed against persons residing within the household sphere, forced sexual intercourse of someone within their household sphere with other persons for commercial purposes and or specific purposes.

Letter d

What is meant by "Economic Neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife and children or family or relatives such as not providing maintenance to the wife or spending the wife's money, not providing or withholding wages of domestic workers and drivers including acts of limiting or prohibiting family members from engaging in decent work.

Letter e

What is meant by "Restriction of movement" is restricting the freedom of movement of the wife or children to develop their potential both for economic jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id and social purposes such as prohibiting gathering or socializing with the community as well as restricting the space of relatives such as preventing domestic workers and drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

CHAPTER III

VICTIMS' RIGHTS

Article 19

In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the community may:

a. form family partners at the village level by the community; b. conduct socialization of women's and children's rights independently; c. provide first aid to victims;
d. participate with the authorized agencies when violence against victims occurs in their environment.
e. community participation shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media. jdih.pakpakbharatkab.go.id
